- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting corrections after strong rallies; if 3 consecutive days >+3% from 14-day moving avg, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights short-term momentum; apply 10–15% discount to forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative over last 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
